title: India's Social Security Net: Navigating Your Retirement Benefits
description: India's "social security" primarily refers to a system of government-backed retirement and welfare schemes, not a single universal benefit like in some Wester.

faq.q: What is India's equivalent of US Social Security retirement benefits?
faq.a: India does not have a single, universal system like the US Social Security. Instead, it offers a multi-layered social security framework for retirement, primarily through the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) for salaried individuals and the National Pension System (NPS) for all citizens, alongside other government pension schemes.

faq.q: Is EPF mandatory for all employees in India?
faq.a: EPF is mandatory for employees earning up to ₹15,000 per month in establishments with 20 or more employees. Those earning above this threshold can opt in voluntarily with employer consent.

faq.q: What are the tax benefits of investing in NPS?
faq.a: Contributions to NPS Tier I are eligible for tax deductions under Section 80C (up to ₹1.5 lakhs) and an additional deduction of up to ₹50,000 under Section 80CCD(1B). The lump sum withdrawal at maturity is tax-exempt up to 60% of the corpus.

faq.q: Can NRIs invest in the National Pension System (NPS)?
faq.a: Yes, Indian citizens, including Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) with a bank account in India and a communication address in the country, are eligible to open an NPS account.

EPF withdrawals are tax-free if an employee has completed five continuous years of service. Premature withdrawals are generally taxable unless specific conditions like ill-health or business closure apply.

faq.q: What is the current interest rate for EPF?
faq.a: For the financial year 2025-26, the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) interest rate has been ratified at 8.25% per annum.

faq.q: What happens to my NPS corpus at retirement?
faq.a: At retirement (typically age 60), you can withdraw a portion of your NPS corpus as a lump sum (up to 80% for non-government subscribers with corpus above ₹12 lakhs, 100% for smaller corpuses), and the remaining amount must be used to purchase an annuity, which provides a regular pension.
